rows.speaker: الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dānī says no explicit transmission establishes imāla for al-Bāriʾ; Ibn Mujāhid inferred it by analogy with the two occurrences in al-Baqara, as Abū al-Fatḥ confirmed.
rows.anchor: وقال الداني في جامعه: لم يذكر أحد عن البارئ نصا

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان الضرير
rows.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Ḍarīr transmits imāla for the al-Māʾida forms, the al-Aʿrāf form, and fala tumāri in al-Kahf; his routes agree explicitly and in performance.
rows.anchor: فروى عنه أبو عثمان الضرير إمالتها وهذا مما اجتمعت عليه الطرق عن أبي عثمان نصا وأداء

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد النصيبي
rows.claim: Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad al-Naṣībī transmits fatḥ for the cited forms, and the source reports no disagreement from him on that transmission.
rows.anchor: وروى فتح الكلمات الثلاث جعفر بن محمد النصيبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī questions al-Shāṭibī’s unique al-Māʾida attribution, saying it follows al-Taysīr as a useful report rather than a reading route relevant to that work.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ذكره الشاطبي رحمه الله ليواري وفأواري في المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-Shāṭibī meant the route of Abū ʿUthmān from al-Dūrī, Ibn al-Jazarī argues it should appear among his isnāds; listing it would also require other omitted disagreements.
rows.anchor: ولو أراد ذكر طريق أبي عثمان عن الدوري لذكرها في أسانيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Dānī’s restriction of Abū ʿUthmān’s imāla to al-Māʾida, excluding al-Aʿrāf, is unique and conflicts with all other transmitters.
rows.anchor: ثم تخصيص المائدة دون الأعراف هو مما انفرد به الداني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī says al-Aʿrāf’s form was transmitted explicitly and in performance by all performance readers; its absence may be a copying loss in al-Fārisī’s book.
rows.anchor: ورواه عنه جميع أصحابه من أهل الأداء نصا وأداء

rows.speaker: الكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read maṭliʿ with kasra on the lām; the other readers read it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي وخلف بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: ابن عامر والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī use ḍamma on the tāʾ, yielding the passive sense ‘you will be shown’; the rest use fatḥa, ‘you will see.’
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر والكسائي بضم التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All read the second tāʾ with fatḥa: they are first shown Hell by angels or others, then see it themselves, as al-Kisāʾī explains.
rows.anchor: ثم لترونها عين اليقين لأن المعنى فيه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وروح
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Rawḥ double the mīm; the remaining readers pronounce it light.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وروح بتشديد الميم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Abū Bakr read ʿumud with ḍamma on both ʿayn and mīm; the others read both with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو بكر بضم العين والميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers use fatḥa on both letters here; ʿamad is the plural of ʿimād, a support or building, glossed as a firm tall structure that keeps an elevated thing from leaning.
rows.anchor: هو بناء محكم مستطيل يمنع المرتفع أن يميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads without yāʾ after hamza, like a triliteral verbal noun; Abū Jaʿfar has yāʾ without hamza, plausibly by replacing the second hamza or by lightening a triliteral form; the others retain hamza plus yāʾ.
rows.anchor: مثل لعلاف مصدر ألف ثلاثيا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads īlāfihim with kasra hamza and no yāʾ; the same is reported from ʿIkrima, Shayba, Ibn ʿUtba, and also from Ibn Kathīr.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بهمزة مكسورة من غير ياء

rows.speaker: أبو علي الواسطي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Wāsiṭī says he had doubts about the attribution of this reading.
rows.anchor: عن أبي علي الواسطي قال: داخلني شك في ذلك

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads hudan wa-raḥmatun with nominative inflection; the other readers use the accusative.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة بالرفع، وقرأ الباقون بالنصب

rows.speaker: يعقوب وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Ḥafṣ read the phrase in the accusative; the rest use the nominative.
rows.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص بالنصب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqūb double the ʿayn without an alif; the others use a light ʿayn preceded by alif.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب بتشديد العين

rows.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو وحفص
rows.claim: The two Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ read the word as masculine plural; the others use a feminine singular form.
rows.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، وأبو عمرو وحفص بفتح العين وهاء مضمومة

rows.speaker: البصريان
rows.claim: The two Basrans read the rāʾ of al-baḥr with accusative inflection; the other readers use the nominative.
rows.anchor: فقرأ البصريان بنصب الراء، وقرأ الباقون بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Ḥafṣ read qāla with an alif as a statement; the others read qul as a command. Ibn al-Jazarī corrects al-Hudhalī and Abū al-ʿAlā for omitting Khalaf’s reading.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص قال بألف على الخبر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the phrase without the initial wāw; the other readers retain it.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ألم بغير واو

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads with tāʾ, a kasra on mīm, and accusative al-ṣumma; the other readers use yāʾ, fatḥa on mīm, and nominative al-ṣummu.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر بتاء مضمومة وكسر الميم

rows.speaker: المدنيان
rows.claim: The two Medinans put the lām of mithqāl in the nominative in both verses; the other readers use the accusative in both.
rows.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان برفع اللام في الموضعين

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads jidhādhan with kasra on the jīm; the other readers use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي بكسر الجيم، وقرأ الباقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ use tāʾ; Abū Bakr and Ruways transmit nūn; the remaining readers use yāʾ.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحفص بالتاء على التأنيث

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the verb with yāʾ in ḍamma and dāl in fatḥa; the others read nūn in fatḥa and dāl in kasra.
rows.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب بالياء مضمومة وفتح الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr use one nūn with doubled jīm, explained as deleting one nūn for ease; others retain two nūns. Grammarians dispute the original second nūn, noting nūn-to-jīm assimilation is rare.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر بنون واحدة وتشديد الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ opens the yāʾ in all six occurrences; Abū Bakr agrees at the Hūd occurrence, and al-Bazzī agrees at the last Luqmān occurrence, yā bunayya aqimi al-ṣalāh.
rows.anchor: روى حفص بفتح الياء في الستة

rows.speaker: قنبل
rows.claim: Qunbul lightens and gives sukūn to the yāʾ in the final Luqmān occurrence.
rows.anchor: وخفف الياء وسكنها فيه، قنبل

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr lightens and gives sukūn to the yāʾ in the first Luqmān occurrence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير الأول من لقمان وهو (يا بني لا تشرك) بتخفيف الياء وإسكانها

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr has no disagreement on the middle Luqmān occurrence: its yāʾ is doubled and kasra-marked; the other readers use that form across all six occurrences.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف عنه في كسر الياء مشددة في الحرف الأوسط

rows.speaker: يعقوب والكسائي
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb and al-Kisāʾī read ʿamila with kasra on mīm and accusative ghayra; the others use a fatḥa on mīm and nominative endings.
rows.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب والكسائي، (عمل) بكسر الميم وفتح اللام

rows.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وابن عامر
rows.claim: The two Medinans, Ibn Kathīr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read with an open lām and doubled nūn; most others use a still lām and light nūn, with further nūn-vowel and yāʾ-presence variants noted.
rows.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، وابن كثير وابن عامر بفتح اللام وتشديد النون

rows.speaker: الداجوني وهبة الله بن سلامة والحلواني
rows.claim: Among Hishām’s transmitters, al-Dājūnī has an open nūn, except Hibat Allāh b. Salāma reports kasra from him, as does al-Ḥulwānī; further variants concern nūn and yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير والداجوني عن أصحابه عن هشام بفتح النون

rows.speaker: المدنيان والكسائي
rows.claim: The two Medinans and al-Kisāʾī use fatḥa on the mīm in both phrases; the other readers use kasra.
rows.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، والكسائي بفتح الميم فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb, Ḥamza, and Ḥafṣ read Thamūd without tanwīn in all four locations; Abū Bakr joins them at the Najm location, while the other readers use tanwīn.
rows.anchor: يعقوب، وحمزة وحفص ثمود في الأربعة، وبغير تنوين

rows.speaker: أبو علي العطار
rows.claim: A unique route through Abū ʿAlī al-ʿAṭṭār transmits two faces at the Najm occurrence, one without tanwīn and one with it.
rows.anchor: وانفرد أبو علي العطار شيخ ابن سوار عن الكناني عن الحربي عن ابن عون عن الصريفيني عن يحيى عنه فيه بوجهين، أحدهما عدم التنوين، والثاني بالتنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers who use tanwīn stop with alif, while those without tanwīn stop without it; one exceptional route from Ḥafṣ stops with alif despite no tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وكل من نون وقف بالألف، ومن لم ينون وقف بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a hamza in these waw or yāʾ contexts has no separate written shape, the rasm can reflect gemination, a dialect that drops hamza, or allow both retaining and deleting it.
rows.anchor: على لغة من يسقط الهمزة رأسا، أو لتحتمل القراءتين إثباتا وحذفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the plural sayyiʾāt, hamza is omitted because of gemination; an alif replaces it despite the usual feminine-plural spelling, while the singular keeps its hamza shape and al-munshaʾāt combines both shapes.
rows.anchor: حذفوها من (سيات) في الجمع نحو (كفر عنهم سياتهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a hamza with ḍamma after kasra, as in wa-lā yunabbiʾuka and sanaqriʾuka, the rasm uses yāʾ according to al-Akhfash rather than the customary waw.
rows.anchor: فلم يرسم على مذهب الجادة بواو، بل رسم على مذهب الأخفش بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The converse forms suʾila and suʾilū are written by the customary rule rather than al-Akhfash’s rule.
rows.anchor: ورسم عكسه سئل وسئلوا على مذهب الجادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manuscripts vary on these open hamzas after fatḥa: some retain alif as expected, while most omit it for simplification when its place is clear.
rows.anchor: فرسمت في بعض المصاحف بالألف على القياس، وحذفت في أكثرها على غير قياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Codices differ on retaining or omitting hamza in arayta and related forms; though some restrict deletion to Sūrat al-Dīn or one other form, Ibn al-Jazarī prefers applying the variation throughout the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: والصحيح إجراء الخلاف في الجميع، والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rasm of naʾā uses only nūn and alif to permit both readings; the fixed alif represents hamza, while the inflected alif is deleted when the two alifs meet.
rows.anchor: فإنه رسم بنون وألف فقط؛ ليحتمل القراءتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāʾ is written with alif as hamza’s shape; in two Najm occurrences an added yāʾ reflects the imāla pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وكذلك رأى كتب في جميع القرآن براء وألف لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In raʾā al-qamar, the fixed alif is the written shape of hamza and the following alif is omitted for abbreviation due to identical letters, not to avoid two sukūns.
rows.anchor: فإن الألف فيه هي صورة الهمزة، والألف بعدها حذفت اختصارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spelling of the Najm form with yāʾ proves the omitted alif was removed for abbreviation; its omission in forms not followed by sukūn shows it was not removed to avoid two sukūns.
rows.anchor: والدليل على حذفها اختصارا للتماثل إثباتها ياء في حرف النجم كما قدمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written alif was deleted for abbreviation because of matching letters, not to avoid two sukūns; the proposed attribution of tarāy to Hishām is also unsound.
rows.anchor: كما زعم في (تراي) وليس في ذلك شيء يصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third deletion face based on some codices is invalid for ashmazzat, iṭmaʾannū, amlaʾanna, and related forms; al-Kisāʾī’s sound report for arayta does not transfer to other readers.
rows.anchor: فقد حكي فيها وجه ثالث، وهو الحذف على رسم بعض المصاحف، وليس بصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An open hamza after kasra or ḍamma is replaced by the corresponding long vowel in one valid face; the reported between-between facilitation is unsound.
rows.anchor: وأما المفتوح بعد كسر وبعد ضم فلا إشكال في إبدال همزته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For hamza with ḍamma after fatḥa in raʾūf and tuʾizzuhum, the single valid face is between-between; the reported waw-with-ḍamma alternative based on rasm is invalid.
rows.anchor: ونحوه فيه وجه واحد، وهو بين بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar has a deletion face in yaṭaʾūna and related forms; deletion in yuʾdihi and by analogy yuʾsan fits the rasm and is preferred by those following it, while waw substitution is rejected.
rows.anchor: وهو الحذف كقراءة أبي جعفر، نص عليه الهذلي وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For hamza with ḍamma after ḍamma in bi-ruʾūsikum and ruʾūs al-shayāṭīn, the choices are between-between or deletion; deletion is preferred by readers following the rasm.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان: بين بين على القياس والثاني الحذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With hamza after kasra and ḍamma, the majority use between hamza and waw; al-Akhfash’s yāʾ substitution is preferred by al-Dānī and others following the rasm.
rows.anchor: أحدهما بين بين، أي: بين الهمزة والواو على مذهب سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Facilitation between hamza and yāʾ and replacement by waw are cited but rejected; al-Dānī prefers deletion with ḍamma before waw where hamza is followed by waw.
rows.anchor: وهو الوجه المعضل كما تقدم، وحكي وجه رابع

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dānī and readers following the rasm prefer deletion with ḍamma on the preceding letter when hamza is followed by waw.
rows.anchor: وهو المختار عند أبي عمرو الداني، ومن أخذ باتباع الرسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using kasra before the waw is a weak face; of the six proposed readings, only three are sound, including facilitation between hamza and waw and deletion options.
rows.anchor: وذكر فيه كسر ما قبل الواو، وهو الوجه الخامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When stopping creates two consecutive sukūns in forms like yastahziʾūn, any valid reading may take madd, tawassuṭ, or qaṣr.
rows.anchor: فيجوز في كل وجه من الأوجه المذكورة كل من الثلاثة الأوجه من المد والتوسط والقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿIzz al-Qalānisī reports replacing the hamza with waw in yuʾdihi and analogues; Ibn al-Jazarī says this face is baseless.
rows.anchor: ذكره أبو العز القلانسي، وقال ليس بشيء

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Ḥafṣ read tanṣīl with fatḥa on the lām; the others read it with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص بنصب اللام

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads fa-ʿazaznā with a light zāy; all other readers double it.
rows.anchor: فروى أبو بكر بتخفيف الزاي وقرأ الباقون بتشديدها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the second hamza with fatḥa and follows his usual rule for facilitation and separation; the other readers use kasra and follow their own rules.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بفتح الهمزة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar lightens the kāf in dhukkirtum; al-Hudhalī uniquely transmits a doubled kāf from Ibn Jamāz, as the other readers read it.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بتخفيف الكاف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads kāna as complete with rafʿ ṣayḥatun, ‘only one blast occurred’; the others treat kāna as incomplete and use naṣb, ‘the seizure was only one blast.’
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بالرفع فيهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All agree on naṣb in mā yanẓurūna illā ṣayḥatan because ṣayḥatan is the object of yanẓurūna.
rows.anchor: على نصب ما ينظرون إلا صيحة إذ هو مفعول ينظرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Abū Bakr omit the object pronoun hāʾ, matching Kūfan codices; the others include it, matching their codices, and Ibn Kathīr joins it.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وروح
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Rawḥ read the rāʾ in qaddarnāhu with ḍamma; the others read it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وروح برفع الراء

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم الهذلي
rows.claim: Al-Hudhalī and other authorities report imāla from al-Sūsī through named routes; other routes preserve it for particular forms, including narā Allāh and sayarā Allāh.
rows.anchor: وقطع به أيضا للسوسي أبو القاسم الهذلي في كامله من طريق أبي عمران

rows.speaker: ابن جمهور
rows.claim: Ibn Jumhūr and others transmit fatḥ from al-Sūsī, the reading most authors record; al-Dānī read it from Ibn Ghalbūn, and its prominence reflects Ibn Jarīr’s independent preference for fatḥ, though both faces are sound.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن جمهور، وغيره عن السوسي الفتح، وهو الذي لم يذكر أكثر المؤلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāʾ takes imāla when an alif follows; after a connecting deletion the imāla remains, but not when jussive deletion removes the alif originally, as in awalam yara al-insān.
rows.anchor: أولم ير الإنسان لعدم وجود الألف بعد الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāʾ is singled out for imāla because its heaviness and strength from trilling distinguish it among letters that are inherently pronounced emphatically.
rows.anchor: من أجل ثقل الراء وقوتها بالتكرير تخصيصها من بين الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author permits rare analogy when it conflicts with no explicit transmission, consensus, or principle, citing inferred idghām in māliyah halak and qāla rajul/rajulān by analogy with qāla rabb.
rows.anchor: ونقل (كتابيه اني) وإدغام (ماليه هلك) قياسا عليه

rows.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Makkī divides readings into three groups: documented transmission, orally acquired readings absent from books, and the smallest group inferred by analogy when no transmission exists.
rows.anchor: فجميع ما ذكرناه في هذا الكتاب ينقسم ثلاثة أقسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī rejects extending analogy indiscriminately from transmitted to untransmitted or from weak to strong readings, including showing the converted mīm of nūn and tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقد زل بسبب ذلك قوم وأطلقوا قياس ما لا يروى على ما روي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects claims to lighten a still rāʾ before kasra or yāʾ without a transmitted basis.
rows.anchor: وقطع بعض القراء بترقيق الراء الساكنة قبل الكسرة والياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects lightening the lām of the divine name by analogy with the light rāʾ in dhikr Allāh.
rows.anchor: وإجازة بعض من بلغنا عنه ترقيق لام الجلالة

rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Sakhāwī says mixing variant readings is an error.
rows.anchor: الإمام أبو الحسن علي بن محمد السخاوي في كتابه جمال القراء:

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawī says to stay with one of the seven readings while the discourse remains connected; after it ends one may switch, though maintaining one reading throughout the session is preferable.
rows.anchor: الحبر العلامة أبو زكريا النووي في كتابه التبيان:

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الجعبري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ gives the same sense; al-Jaʿbarī says combining readings is forbidden within a word or across connected words, and otherwise disliked.
rows.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الجعبري: والتركيب ممتنع في كلمة وفي كلمتين

rows.speaker: الآمدي
rows.claim: A report in al-Furūʿ says not to recite al-Fātiḥa and five verses of al-Baqara; al-Āmidī explains the restriction as applying before supplication, while another view recommends the practice.
rows.anchor: قال الآمدي يعني قبل الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī interprets Aḥmad’s ‘no’ as forbidding the extra recitation before supplication; supplication should follow Sūrat al-Nās, though another report from Aḥmad recommends it.
rows.anchor: يكون دعاؤه عقيب قراءة سورة الناس

rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Sakhāwī asks how the report that no deed saves from Hell more than remembrance of God fits with the report that the Qurʾān is the best remembrance.
rows.anchor: قال السخاوي بعد ذكر هذا الحديث: فإن قيل

rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Sakhāwī answers that the Qurʾān is remembrance because it praises God and recounts His mercy, power, creation, care, guidance, laws, and the fates of opponents; all of it is His speech.
rows.anchor: القرآن من ذكر الله إذ فيه الثناء على الله عز وجل ومدحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites sound reports naming faith, jihad, pilgrimage, prayer, honoring parents, patience, generosity, and fasting among the best deeds.
rows.anchor: ورد في هذا المعنى أحاديث صحيحة منها أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One harmonization takes ‘best’ to mean one among several deeds in the highest rank, rather than a single exclusive deed.
rows.anchor: إن المراد أي من أفضل الأعمال النظائر
